## How the score was worked out

Each result implies a score on its own, after adjusting for how hard that test is and who ran it. The model's score is their weighted average, with a small pull toward the middle for thinly tested models. Each test's weight is its *counts* column above; here it is added up by who ran the tests. [Method](../method.md)

<pre>
source                                    results  share of the score
<a name="first-party-qwen-scores"></a><a href="https://arxiv.org/pdf/2511.21631v2#page=18">Qwen (lab)</a>                                     25   95% ▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇▇
<a name="paper-2606.01348v3-chartarena"></a><a href="https://arxiv.org/html/2606.01348v3">ChartArena: Benchmarking Chart Parsing …</a>        1    3% ▇
<a name="paper-2608.17895v1-bear-bench"></a><a href="https://arxiv.org/html/2608.17895v1">BEAR-Bench: A Bilingual Enterprise and …</a>        1    2% ▇
prior: pull toward the middle                        0% ▇
weighted average                                   = 56.3
</pre>

## How to run it

### llama.cpp (recommended)

1. Install llama.cpp. Homebrew and winget installs name the commands llama-cli and llama-server instead. [Other ways to install](https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/blob/master/docs/install.md)
   
   ```sh
   # macOS / Linux
   curl -LsSf https://llama.app/install.sh | sh
   # Windows
   irm https://llama.app/install.ps1 | iex
   ```

2. Run Qwen3-VL 4B Thinking (Q4_K_M, needs ~2.5 GB, from [huggingface.co/Qwen](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking-GGUF/tree/a55c03cbb1dad5a0c678efa066a8dbccf5a8d30e))
   
   ```sh
   llama cli -hf Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking-GGUF:Q4_K_M
   ```

3. Or start a local server and open the address it prints (http://localhost:9931)
   
   ```sh
   llama serve -hf Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking-GGUF:Q4_K_M
   ```

Other versions: Q8_0 (~4.3 GB) `llama cli -hf Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking-GGUF:Q8_0`

### LM Studio

1. Install LM Studio. Open the app once before using the lms command. [Download it (macOS / Windows / Linux)](https://lmstudio.ai/download)

2. Run Qwen3-VL 4B Thinking (Q4_K_M, needs ~2.5 GB, from [huggingface.co/Qwen](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking-GGUF/tree/a55c03cbb1dad5a0c678efa066a8dbccf5a8d30e))
   
   ```sh
   lms get https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking-GGUF@Q4_K_M -y
   ```

3. Then run lms ls to see its name, and lms chat followed by that name

Other versions: Q8_0 (~4.3 GB) `lms get https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking-GGUF@Q8_0 -y` · 4bit (~3.1 GB, Mac only) `lms get https://huggingface.co/lmstudio-community/Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking-MLX-4bit -y` · 8bit (~5.1 GB, Mac only) `lms get https://huggingface.co/lmstudio-community/Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking-MLX-8bit -y`

### Ollama

1. Install Ollama. [Download it (macOS / Windows)](https://ollama.com/download)
   
   ```sh
   # Linux
   curl -fsSL https://ollama.com/install.sh | sh
   ```

2. Run Qwen3-VL 4B Thinking (Q4_K_M, needs ~3.3 GB, from [ollama.com](https://ollama.com/library/qwen3-vl/tags))
   
   ```sh
   ollama run qwen3-vl:4b-thinking
   ```

Other versions: Q8_0 (~5.1 GB) `ollama run qwen3-vl:4b-thinking-q8_0`

### MLX (Mac)

1. Install MLX (Mac). Apple silicon Macs only, text only.
   
   ```sh
   # with uv
   uv tool install mlx-lm
   # or
   pip install mlx-lm
   ```

2. Run Qwen3-VL 4B Thinking (4bit, needs ~3.1 GB, Mac only, from [huggingface.co/lmstudio-community](https://huggingface.co/lmstudio-community/Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking-MLX-4bit/tree/f90f31f2561a8eb79a1b9aabc757d5b5682527ff))
   
   ```sh
   mlx_lm.chat --model lmstudio-community/Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking-MLX-4bit
   ```

3. Or start an OpenAI-compatible server at http://localhost:8080/v1
   
   ```sh
   mlx_lm.server --model lmstudio-community/Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking-MLX-4bit
   ```

Other versions: 8bit (~5.1 GB, Mac only) `mlx_lm.chat --model lmstudio-community/Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking-MLX-8bit`

Official weights and documentation: [huggingface.co/Qwen](https://huggingface.co/Qwen/Qwen3-VL-4B-Thinking)
